name: resting_posture_01
question: Can a feedback policy maintain stable seated or leaning support with less whole-body motor effort across feasible surface geometries?

method.learner: PPO, first with sensor history and joint-position targets under existing actuator limits
method.motion_ownership: Trainable joint targets; no frozen timed sitting generator in the control path
method.initialization: Physically settled supported states captured from valid trajectories, then perturbed without penetrations
method.optional_teacher: Constrained static posture/contact-force optimization for feasible reset examples, initialization and a model-based comparison; do not delay the first horizontal seated baseline for this solver
method.why_not_only_imitation: Existing demonstrations need not be the lowest-effort postures; imitation can initialize, task reward should improve them
method.why_not_vla: No language interpretation is needed for this first contact and balance skill
method.ground_truth: Reset construction and training reward/evaluation labels only; no privileged actor or estimator input; critic sensor-only in the first study

success_definition.task: Remain supported on an intended pelvis, thigh or approved back patch, with feet allowed to bear load; stable useful torso orientation, no slipping, forbidden contacts, limit violation or fall
success_definition.effort: All-joint mean squared torque divided by declared joint reference ratings, plus per-joint/leg/torso reports; prefer continuous ratings when available
success_definition.energy_limitation: Torque-based effort is a proxy, not measured electrical energy. Mechanical power alone is inadequate for stationary holding. Do not invent current, resistance or thermal parameters.
success_definition.leaning: Support is measured along the observed surface normal; no requirement for the surface to lift 75 percent of body weight or for the feet to unload
success_definition.constraints_before_economy: Lower effort counts as an improvement only when full-duration support, slip and perturbation performance are retained
success_definition.minimum_claim: Lower-effort robust posture among tested policies; no claim of a global minimum

curriculum.surface: Wide rigid horizontal support; feasibility-checked heights and randomized supported initial poses
curriculum.goal: Learn to remain seated, adjust posture and reduce whole-body holding effort; no standing-to-sitting requirement yet
Retain physical support and traction as normal direction changes; use the same full 3D geometry/contact contract
Use suitable hip/back contacts with feet on the floor; test friction, allowed contact patches and full force/moment balance
Progressively initialize farther from contact, ultimately connect standing/approach to the learned resting behavior

feasibility: Candidate heights and angles are proposals, not certified reachable states. Test collision clearance, joint margin, friction, force/moment balance and dynamic settling. Log every rejected candidate separately; report both reset coverage and hold success.

pilot_design.status: Proposed after simulator smoke validation and current capped-impact comparison; not queued
pilot_design.budget_limitation: A bounded pilot, not enough evidence of convergence or general sitting/leaning skill; profile throughput before fixing later budgets
baselines: Same valid initial posture held by fixed PD joint targets
Optional optimized posture plus feedback, once implemented
pilot_design.evaluation: Same held-out height/start combinations and disturbance schedules for both seeds/arms; full 20-second holds and separate 60-second confirmation on finalists, no success-by-early-reset
metrics: peak joint effort and sustained near-limit time
pilot_design.comparison_rule: Report every attempt, same-case paired effort on common successes, and failures separately. A lower-effort policy with worse stability is a tradeoff, not a win. Keep both training seeds.

inputs: depth-derived local support plane, bounded patch, relative body pose, validity and age
actor_contract.normal_convention: Unit surface normal oriented from the surface toward the robot; preserve full orientation and local patch bounds
actor_contract.contact_policy: Feet on floor plus identified pelvis/thigh/back support patches; hands/arms are outside the initial scope

implementation_audit.finding: reset_seats places yaw-only level surfaces; a new full-orientation fixture adapter is needed
support_fraction uses positive world-Z normal force on pelvis/thigh contacts; inappropriate as the sole leaning support metric
horizontal_planes filters abs(normal_z) > 0.96; support association also assumes near-parallel floor/seat planes
initial seat anchor is horizontal and association contains two-degree normal gates; steep surfaces are not currently tracked
standing resets, pelvis height above level seat and small corrections to a frozen timed generator are unsuitable for a general resting task

implemented_this_turn: CPU behavioral tests including inclined and vertical contact examples
still_required_before_training: Capture and dynamically validate complete seated reset states; do not infer omitted root/joint velocities from sparse pose archives
Wire total contact forces including tangential friction, allowed patches and slip into reward/evaluation labels, verify their signs and units
Separate runtime sensor observations from reset/reward truth and provide full trainable joint targets
Run fixed-PD baseline and deterministic perturbed-hold smoke cases, inspect trajectories and contact labels
For incline stages, implement full surface pose spawning and observed oblique-plane association before enabling that stage
preservation: All existing controllers/checkpoints and the active support_capped_impact_01 study remain unchanged. This specification does not start or schedule training.

references.use: Primary evidence for optimization-based multi-contact force/posture control on a position-controlled humanoid; not evidence for this G1 resting task
Primary example of constrained RL for energy-related objectives in humanoid walking; supports considering explicit constraints, not a guarantee for resting
